newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's May open unemployment falls to 3.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's May open unemployment falls to 3.9 pct.

text.p: Mexico's open, or base, unemployment rate fell to 3.90 percent during May compared to 4.29 percent in April, the National Statistics Institute INEGI said on Wednesday.
INEGI said in a statement the jobless rate was the lowest in almost 2-1/2 years, and compared with 5.4 percent in May 1996.
INEGI said the drop coincided with employment data from the Mexican Social Security Institute, that showed a 9.1 percent increase in jobs in May.
The employment rate was lower than the 4.12 percent predicted in the latest Reuters survey of economists. Interacciones had the closest forecast of those polled.
INEGI defines open unemployment as members of the workforce older than 12 who have searched for work but have not worked more than one hour a week during a month.
The Rate of General Pressure, which measures those in work looking for a new job as well as open unemployment, was 7.0 percent during May compared to 8.0 percent during April.

The Rate of Partial Joblessness and Unemployment, which includes open unemployment and those who have worked less than 35 hours a week due to market conditions, fell to 8.5 percent during May versus 9.7 percent in April.
The Alternative Open Unemployment Rate, which includes open unemployment as well as those who have given up looking for work, was 4.8 percent in May compared to 5.2 percent in April.
